utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will the Registrar call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-02-65-PT, the Prosecutor versus Zeljko Mejakic, Momcilo Gruban, Dusan Fustar, and Dusko Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May we have the appearances for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: May it please, Your Honours, Sureta Chana, Nick Koumjian for the Prosecution, assisted by Ruth Karper, the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Chana. For the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Jovan Simic, attorney from Belgrade for Mr. Mejakic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TURLAKOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, attorney Sanja Turlakov for Mr. Momcilo Gruban.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Attorney Dragan Ivetic from Chicago, representing the accused Dusan Fustar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Attorney Slobodanka Nedic from Belgrade for Dusko Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a Status Conference pursuant to Rule 65 bis. We have a number of issues to deal with and I will go through them in the -- in a particular order and call on counsel as appropriate. I start first with Pre-Trial motions. The Prosecution had filed a motion for protective measures in relation to its required disclosure for the accused Mejakic. I understand that the Mejakic Defence has confirmed that they have no objection to the relief sought and will not be filing a response to the motion. The Chamber will therefore be in a position to issue an order shortly. This should be ready certainly prior to the break next week, Friday. The only other pending matter is a filing from the Gruban Defence on the 30th of May addressing possible agreed facts. This is really a matter that ought not to be the subject of a motion, at any rate at this time, and it is for the parties to continue their discussions on this subject. I understand that this has been passed on to the parties and that work is being done on the agreed facts. I want to look now at the impact of the arrival of the accused Mejakic on the trial. In this regard, the conference is facilitated by the work done at the 65 ter conference. It's clear that there would be a need for the Prosecution to supplement its pre-trial brief. I understand that that has been confirmed. In connection with the question of the criminal responsibility of Mejakic, and additionally the Prosecution would be adding a schedule detailing the specific events relating to Mejakic. In light of all of this, I'm going to set out the timetable as follows: The 6th of August, Prosecution disclosure of Rule 66(A)(1) material to be completed. 20th of August, the Prosecution to file the schedule relating to Mejakic. The 19th of September, the Mejakic Defence to file preliminary motions. And the 3rd of October for any response from the Prosecution to the preliminary motions. As far as disclosure is concerned, that has been done both for 66(A)(1) and(2) in relation to the accused Fustar, Gruban, and Knezevic. And also for Rule 68. As far as Mejakic is concerned, my understanding is that the -- in fact, 66(A)(1) disclosure would have been done by the 22nd, yesterday. Ms. Chana, is that so?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: The Prosecution can confirm that it was posted to Belgrade, and I believe it will be there in three days' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. And the only thing outstanding then would be 68 and you're conducting searches.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have to revisit our binders again to look for Rule 68 for -- specifically now for Mejakic. We are doing the searches. We are also looking at it in house and we should be able to disclose the first batch of it at least within the next two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That would be very good, in view of the conclusion that I will have at the end of this session. Pre-Trial briefs, we have already noted that the Prosecution may wish to supplement its brief after the preliminary motions. And the Defence Pre-Trial briefs are already in for the other accuseds, Gruban, Knezevic, and Fustar. 92 bis, I understand, Ms. Chana, that the assessment of your office is that most of the statements go to the acts and conduct of the accused.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Most of our statements do go to the acts and the conduct of the accused and this is again where I go back to our agreed facts. And if we are to come to some sort of reasonable conclusion, then we will not -- we will be able to streamline our witness list a little bit more, which we are always trying to do as our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I also understand that what you're proposing to do in light of that was to submit transcripts of 38 witnesses who have already testified.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We are intending to do just that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, can I encourage you to have a look again at the statements to see whether they are susceptible to the 92 bis(A) regime? And in fact, the Chamber itself will have a look at this to see whether any of the statements can in fact be addressed by 92 bis. Agreed facts, I understand that discussions have been held with the Fustar and Knezevic Defence teams, and that discussion has resulted in a limited number of facts being agreed, and that the Gruban Defence is willing to accept those facts. The parties are still working on this matter and I encourage them to continue. Adjudicated facts, work needs to be done on that. I understand work has started on that and I encourage the parties to try to reach agreement on agreed -- on adjudicated facts. Ms. Chana, you had indicated earlier that your case could be presented in about six weeks. Would you have the same estimate in the light of the arrival of Mejakic?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, seeing that one of the other accused is no longer within this, I think we would still confirm about six weeks would be the length of the Prosecution trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What I wanted to say, and what I hinted at about this case, is that all parties should be in a state of readiness for trial sometime in the autumn, if called upon. I can't say with any certainty that the case will be tried, but parties should keep themselves in a state of readiness for trial. And the question as to what would happen in that event to the accused Mejakic is something that would have to be dealt with in the light of the circumstances at that time. And those circumstances would obviously have to take account of the need to ensure that the accused Mejakic has enough time to prepare for trial. Does anyone wish to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would state at this point that the Prosecution's view would be that we would like to have the accused tried together, and every endeavour I think should be made to do that. And I think the Trial Chamber is obviously sensitive to the issues involved at this point of severing any of the accused. So this would be the Prosecution's view, that Mejakic, we should try to bring him up to speed so all the accused can be tried together at the same time. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We are very sensitive to that and I believe that that would certainly be the best option. It would certainly be the best option. I can't say with any certainty that that will be the outcome, but it would obviously be the best option. Mr. Simic? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to inform you and the Prosecution that the Defence will by no means obstruct the schedule that you set. We shall do everything in order to be prepared for trial when you are prepared. If we should not have enough time, but if our time is not drastically shortened, we would accept to start with the trial if we were allowed to present evidence. We will do everything in order to be prepared for trial when you decide that the trial should start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Simic, for your spirit of cooperation. There are many strategies that can be employed and that are open to Trial Chambers to deal with a matter of this kind. But at the -- at the bottom, of course, we have in mind that the question of fairness to all the accused. May I at this time then ask any of the accused whether there is any matter that they would wish to raise concerning the case itself, the arrangements for the case or their conditions of detention? Mr. Gruban? Is there anything that you wish to say either through your counsel or -- Gruban is not here of course, yes, yes. Mr. Knezevic? THE ACCUSED KENEZEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have nothing that I would like to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Knezevic. Mr. Fustar? THE ACCUSED FUSTAR: [Interpretation] I would like to thank the Trial Chamber for allowing me to go and visit my father's grave. I have nothing else to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Fustar. And Mr. Mejakic? THE ACCUSED MEJAKIC: [Interpretation] There is nothing in particular I would like to say. There are no issues I would like to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have to fix a date for the next Status Conference. The Senior Legal Officer? Ms. Chana?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. Just for the sake of absolute certainty, I just recall that when you said six weeks for our case and I think that I've said it previously, six weeks if indeed we have a streamlined case in the sense of adjudicated facts and the agreed facts. In the events we do not come to an agreement on much of these factors, that will increase the Prosecution time. I just want to leave that open, just to be quite clear. This is not definitively taken as six weeks in all circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I think you're quite right to make that clarification. That's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'll fix Wednesday, the 12th, as the date for the next -- the 12th of November, as the date for the next Status Conference. Is there any other matter that any party would wish to raise? If not, then the hearing is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
